rationale: Built the event that makes the liveness measurement non-vacuous, and it cost one real failure worth recording. The persist/apply step now skips a randomly chosen node about one time in six, so a committed configuration change can genuinely stay unapplied at that node; the draft-side run then reports unapplied_conf_change_states=48 (the antecedent now holds at 48 of 3600 check points) together with stalled_states=0, i.e. in every state where some node held a committed-but-unapplied configuration change at least one node was still promotable. The first version of this revision panicked - '1 state.commit 5 is out of range [0, 4]' from loadState at a restart event - because a node whose application lagged could hold a committed index beyond the entries its storage had received, so writing its hard state made newRaft reject it; flushing that node's committed entries to storage before recording the hard state fixed it, and that ordering is itself the application duty Storage's contract implies. Also still holds with lag present: 262 configuration changes, 429 restarts, 470 elections, 461 ordinary proposals, violations=0. These draft-side numbers are construction feedback only, so the experiment below requests isolated execution of these bytes.

scope.description: Ninth revision of the same fixed harness; probes A, B and C are unchanged. The sweep adds application lag: the per-step persist/apply pass now skips a randomly chosen node about one time in six, so that node's applied index stays behind its committed index and a committed configuration change can remain unapplied there. The liveness witness then has its antecedent, and the summary reports unapplied_conf_change_states (how many check points had a node with a committed-but-unapplied configuration change) alongside stalled_states (how many of those had no promotable node), plus seeds, steps, elections, ordinary proposals, conf_change_proposals, restarts and violations; when the witness fires it also emits up to three liveness_witness events carrying per-node state, term, applied, committed, has_unapplied, promotable and in_config. Restart events now flush the node's committed entries to storage before recording its hard state, because a node with application lag can hold a committed index beyond its stored log and newRaft rejects such a hard state.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, hasUnappliedConfChanges, promotable, newRaft, SetHardState); no production logic is modified.
Application lag is produced by not running the apply step for a node, which is what a slow or stalled application looks like to raft; the node's own log is still replicated normally.
The restart event is well formed by construction: entries are flushed before the hard state is recorded, so the restarted instance's commit index is within its stored log.
Randomness is fixed per seed; counts over a fixed seed set are descriptive, not rates.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup on a random node, MsgProp with a tagged payload, tick() on a random node, isolate a random node, recover, TransferLeader from a random voter to the current leader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change on node 4, half the time JointImplicit), a restart of a random node from its persisted hard state and applied ConfState, or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 but skip a randomly chosen node about one time in six, then evaluate the four invariants and the liveness witness, finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary with all counters.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and sweep case as the previous execution, with application lag added - the per-step apply pass skips a random node about one time in six - and the restart event fixed to flush entries before recording the hard state. The added event is what gives the liveness witness its antecedent; fresh execution is requested because the harness bytes and the event set changed.
